misconception_description: Confusing a class definition with an instantiated object
learner_response_example: A class allocates memory before you create anything.
recommended_intervention: Clarify that a class is a blueprint; an object is created when Java executes new ClassName().

misconception_description: Thinking every variable of a class type already contains an object
learner_response_example: Student s; already made the Student object.
recommended_intervention: Contrast a null reference or declaration with a constructed instance.

misconception_description: Believing private means data can never be safely exposed
learner_response_example: If a field is private nobody can read it.
recommended_intervention: Show how getters expose controlled access while direct field mutation remains blocked.

misconception_description: Using public fields and calling it encapsulation
learner_response_example: The field is public so it is easier and still encapsulated.
recommended_intervention: Explain that encapsulation protects state through private fields and controlled methods.

misconception_description: Using inheritance for any code reuse even without an is-a relationship
learner_response_example: A Car should inherit Engine because it uses one.
recommended_intervention: Contrast is-a inheritance with has-a composition before continuing.

misconception_description: Thinking private parent fields are directly accessible in child classes
learner_response_example: The subclass can use the private balance field directly.
recommended_intervention: Explain inherited behavior versus direct private field access.

misconception_description: Thinking return type alone overloads a method
learner_response_example: int total() and double total() are overloaded.
recommended_intervention: Emphasize that Java overloading requires a different parameter list.

misconception_description: Confusing overloaded methods with overridden methods
learner_response_example: Two same-name methods anywhere are overriding.
recommended_intervention: Separate compile-time signature selection from subclass replacement.

misconception_description: Confusing method overriding with method overloading
learner_response_example: Overriding is two methods with different parameters in the same class.
recommended_intervention: Contrast overriding as replacing a parent method with overloading as same-name different parameters.

misconception_description: Thinking @Override changes runtime behavior by itself
learner_response_example: The annotation makes Java call the child method.
recommended_intervention: Explain that matching method signatures enable overriding; the annotation checks intent.

misconception_description: Thinking polymorphism uses the variable type instead of the object type
learner_response_example: Animal a = new Dog() calls Animal sound.
recommended_intervention: Use dynamic dispatch: the actual object type decides the overriding method at runtime.

misconception_description: Thinking polymorphism and inheritance are identical
learner_response_example: Polymorphism just means one class extends another.
recommended_intervention: Show that inheritance enables shared type relationships, while polymorphism is varied runtime behavior through a common type.
